hooks.title: Gen Z oral care boom, August 2026
hooks.why_now: A trade press feature published August 7, 2026 notes that Gen Z is pushing oral care into a mainstream wellness and aesthetics category, with hello's Whipped Toothpaste cited as the leading example of the trend.
hooks.angle: The same cultural moment that has millions of people paying closer attention to what they put in their mouths is a natural opening to ask whether they know their oral cancer risk factors.

hooks.title: National Recovery Month begins
hooks.why_now: September 1 opens National Recovery Month, when conversations about alcohol and substance use surge across health media and social platforms in a consistent, well-documented annual pattern.
hooks.angle: Alcohol is one of the three primary modifiable risk factors for oral cancer, making Recovery Month a direct and honest moment to invite people to complete a free risk questionnaire.

hooks.title: Lancet Americas study: alcohol and oral HPV
hooks.why_now: A 2026 Lancet Americas paper finding that even modest alcohol use may raise susceptibility to oral high-risk HPV infection is being recirculated in health media as Recovery Month coverage begins.
hooks.angle: The study gives OralCheck a specific, peer-reviewed finding to reference when explaining why alcohol is a question on an oral cancer risk assessment.

hooks.title: Labor Day US wellness reset
hooks.why_now: Labor Day reliably generates a wave of new-season wellness content as people plan preventive health habits heading into fall.
hooks.angle: The end-of-summer pause is a natural, low-friction moment to spend five minutes completing a free oral cancer risk questionnaire before the busy fall schedule takes over.

hooks.title: Hispanic Heritage Month opens
hooks.why_now: Hispanic Heritage Month begins September 15 and prompts health organizations to highlight disparities in cancer prevention and screening access.
hooks.angle: Oral cancer screening rates are lower in some Hispanic communities, and a free, accessible online questionnaire is a concrete step toward closing that gap.

hooks.title: Stoptober quit-smoking challenge begins
hooks.why_now: NHS England's annual 28-day stop-smoking campaign launches on October 1, driving large-scale public conversation about quitting tobacco in the UK and beyond.
hooks.angle: Tobacco is one of the most significant modifiable risk factors for oral cancer, making Stoptober a direct and credible moment to encourage an oral cancer risk check.

hooks.title: Mouth Cancer Action Month advance awareness
hooks.why_now: November's Mouth Cancer Action Month campaign begins its pre-launch communications in early October, and dental and health publications are already publishing preview coverage.
hooks.angle: Early October is the most credible window to prime audiences that mouth cancer awareness month is weeks away and that a free risk questionnaire is available now.

hooks.title: World Heart Day, September 29
hooks.why_now: World Heart Day is a WHO-backed global awareness date that reliably trends on health channels every September 29.
hooks.angle: Tobacco and heavy alcohol use raise risk for both heart disease and oral cancer, so a day dedicated to reducing those shared risk factors connects honestly to an oral cancer questionnaire.
